snippets.output: Muscle strain is a common injury that can be caused by overuse, overstretching, or direct blows to the muscle.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of causes of muscle strain - parallel properties of one subject.

snippets.output: The duration of pain from muscle strain can vary depending on the severity of the injury and the individual's overall health.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel factors affecting duration of pain - enumeration.

snippets.output: Mild muscle strains typically resolve on their own within 7-14 days.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single-atom standalone fact about mild strain resolution time.

snippets.output: More severe muscle strains may take longer to heal, often requiring 4-6 weeks or more for full recovery.
snippets.pattern_notes: Severity + timeframe for severe strains - properties of one subject.

snippets.output: Factors that can influence the healing time include the location of the strain, the severity of the injury, and the effectiveness of treatment. Strains in the lower back may take longer to heal than those in the upper body.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumeration of healing-time factors plus a specific instance.

snippets.output: If pain from a muscle strain persists or worsens over time, it may be a sign of a more serious underlying condition, such as a herniated disc or a stress fracture. Medical attention should be sought in such cases.
snippets.pattern_notes: Recommendation (seek medical attention) supported by premises about persistent pain indicating serious conditions.
